claims.text: Conventionally rapid-cooled Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 develops multiple primary non-eutectic crystalline phases during solidification.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 has a usable supercooled-liquid temperature interval between Tg and Tx.
An isothermal hold between Tg and Tx after rapid cooling will enhance amorphous retention in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The isothermal hold will increase the alloy's thermal stability.
The isothermal hold will retard primary heterogeneous nucleation and crystallization.
Cooling must be sufficiently rapid to bypass extensive primary crystallization before the isothermal hold.
The hold will produce a more relaxed and homogeneous amorphous matrix.
The hold will reduce residual stresses and atomic-scale heterogeneities that act as primary-phase nucleation sites.
Limited atomic diffusion below Tx will postpone crystalline-phase formation during subsequent reheating.
Held samples will have a higher crystallization-onset temperature than unheld controls.
Held samples will exhibit reduced exothermic crystallization peaks during thermal analysis.
Held samples will retain a larger amorphous fraction than unheld controls.
Unheld conventionally processed samples exhibit multiple exothermic events during reheating and relatively poor glass formation.
The intervention is effective only above a critical cooling rate and within a narrow temperature window between Tg and Tx.
A hold temperature that is too high may accelerate crystallization.

contradictions.description: The proposed relaxation of the amorphous structure requires atomic rearrangement, while the mechanism simultaneously says the hold minimizes local atomic rearrangements; the intended distinction between beneficial relaxation and crystallization-producing rearrangement is not stated.
